summary.headline: TANFAC Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR230 crores (+37% YoY), but gross margin fell to 32.5% from 39%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to about INR230 crores, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with H1 revenue up 21% to about INR418 crores. Gross margin compressed to 32.5% from 39% a year earlier and 37% in Q1, while PAT rose about 11% YoY to INR19 crores. Management attributed the margin dip to higher realizations diluting percentage margins, a roughly 45-day lag in passing through sulphur and fluorspar costs, and early-stage ramp-up of new products. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 35-40% and guided H2 EBITDA margin to about 18%, with HFC-32 commissioning targeted for Q3 FY27.

segments.name: AHF (anhydrous hydrofluoric acid)
segments.commentary: Total AHF capacity is 30,000 MT per annum across two 15,000 MT plants, with H1 FY27 utilisation about 78%. Gross profit per ton stated as stable, with margin % lower due to higher realisations.

segments.name: Solar grade DHF
segments.commentary: Capacity raised from 20,000 to 25,000 MT per annum via debottlenecking at nominal capex; utilisation rose from 80-85% in Q1 to 90-95% in Q2. Pricing is contractual with a roughly 45-day lag on raw material pass-through.

segments.name: HFC-32 (R-32) refrigerant gas
segments.commentary: Plant about 90% complete with about INR360 crores committed (about 90% of project cost); target commissioning Q3 FY27. Guided utilisation about 20% in Q4 FY27, about 95% in FY28, and 90-100% thereafter. Contract price around $7/kg on formula basis, with spot-linked sales for about 35% of volume.

segments.name: New fluorinated inorganic products
segments.commentary: Several new products added in early commercialisation with subdued margins and lower introductory pricing for penetration; management expects their share of H2 volume to rise significantly.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth revised to 35-40% from earlier 30% guidance; FY28 revenue growth guided at 55-60%.
EBITDA margin: H2 FY27 about 18%, full FY27 average about 16%, FY28 about 24-26% with full-year HFC-32 production; separately stated H2 margin range of 15-17% from H2 onwards.
HFC-32 commissioning Q3 FY27, with revenue contribution from Q4 FY27; FY27 HFC-32 volumes estimated at 2,000-3,000 MT.
FY27 total capex about INR440-450 crores, with INR70-80 crores balance remaining in FY27; FY28 minimum capex about INR250 crores for AHF and solar grade expansion.
Expected sulphur price moderation and fluorspar inventory normalisation to 3-4 months within 1-2 quarters; receivable days expected to fall about 15 days from next quarter.
capex_capacity: HFC-32 plant: INR395 crores project, about INR360 crores incurred by September 2026; funded by INR350 crores equity (INR250 crores QIP plus INR100 crores preferential) and about INR50 crores debt.
AHF capacity planned to rise from 30,000 MT to 45,000 MT (third plant, 15,000 MT), without cannibalising external sales.
Solar grade DHF capacity planned to double from 25,000 MT to 50,000 MT in a next expansion; new solar-grade capex estimated at INR90-100 crores per new entrant.
Unutilised issue proceeds of INR157 crores, mainly committed to ongoing projects and expected to be used by end of FY27.
Medium-term greenfield plans for electronic chemicals, fluoropolymers and next-generation gases; priority decision expected in 3-4 months, with a forward-integration announcement possibly in January.
demand_pricing: Solar grade DHF demand cited rising from about 25,000 MT to about 1 lakh MT as Indian solar cell capacity grows from 30 GW to about 100 GW in three years; management sees no near-term competition given capex and about one-year gestation.

R-32 contract price rose from about $5.5/kg to about $7/kg on formula basis; spot prices expected at $6.7-7+ levels. Contract/spot mix about 65:35 to 60:40. Management expects FY28 realisations of $6.5-7.5/kg if raw material costs normalise.
Sulphur prices rose about 5x over a year (about INR25/kg in Nov 2025 to about INR120/kg in Sep 2026), now stable to slightly declining. Management cited 10-15% cost increase across the board.
Q2 revenue growth attributed about 85-87% to realisation and 12-15% to volume; management said volumes grew at least 15% YoY.
Chinese R-32 prices elevated, Indian prices lower, so import activity is minimal; 40,000 MT of new Indian R-32 capacity cited as coming in December.
Fluorspar accounts for about 70% of raw material value; inventory raised to 6-7 months after bulk procurement amid West Asia supply risk.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross and EBITDA margins fall sharply, and how will H2 and FY28 look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross profit per ton was stable and the percentage drop reflects higher realisations. Expected H2 FY27 EBITDA margin about 18%, FY27 about 16%, and FY28 about 24-26% with full-year HFC-32.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 45-day lag in passing on raw material costs the cause of the margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, for solar grade DHF the pass-through lag is about 45 days, while newly introduced products carry lower introductory pricing. Management expects both to benefit as sulphur prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise from 91 to 104?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days rose from 57 to 72 because September was a major billing month; about 70% was collected in October. Inventory rose to 64 days (fluorspar buffer), offset by payables rising to 33 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR50 crore debt-funded portion and remaining capex be sufficient?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding is about INR350 crores equity and about INR50 crores debt for the INR395 crore HFC-32 project. Total FY27 capex is about INR440-450 crores, with INR250 crores minimum for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue growth split and AHF capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 growth of 37% split about 85-87% realisation and 12-15% volume. Of the 31,000-32,000 MT AHF output, about 12,000 MT goes to solar grade and 13,000 MT to R-32, leaving 3,000-5,000 MT for existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from Anupam Rasayan (parent) in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 revenue from the parent was INR2-3 crores, which is not significant.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on sulphur and fluorspar price stabilisation and the 30-45 day pass-through lag; H1 gross margin 32.5% vs 39% last year.
HFC-32 commissioning slippage risk for Q3 FY27; FY27 ramp-up volumes of only 2,000-3,000 MT and 20% utilisation in Q4 are assumed.
Working capital intensity: inventory at 6-7 months of fluorspar, receivable days at 72, and payable build-up that management expects to normalise in 1-2 quarters.
Solar grade expansion (25,000 to 50,000 MT) and a new AHF plant are unannounced, and no back-to-back offtake contract is yet executed for the 5,000 MT debottlenecked volume.
R-32 pricing exposure: about 35% of volume is uncontracted at spot; new Indian R-32 capacity in December could weigh on prices.
Reported ROE fell sharply after equity infusion; adjusted ROE about 18% excluding issue proceeds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the HFC-32 timeline, with specific numeric guidance raised for FY27 revenue. More cautious and less specific on near-term margin recovery, which management ties to raw material price moderation and ramp-up of new products. Management declined to give per-kg spread details and avoided a view on the US market beyond near-term observations.
key_quotes: So we expect EBITDA margins to normalize back to 15% to 16% range from this quarter and with further substantial margin expansion anticipated once our value-added HFC-32 capacity achieves commercialization.
But currently, we see INR250 crores is the minimum capex.
So we can say earlier this -- our guidance of 30% growth for FY27. But looking at the current demand scenario, we are revising our guidance to around 35% to 40% growth for the full year in FY27.
